content: (The location is now Solitude.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Lydia, Serana, chicken, Solitude Guard) (MJR cast the spell / consumed Ostim Scene Shout)

Solitude Guard: Quiet night for patrol. Dibella's moon hangs full and heavy over the lighthouse. Jaree-Ra: Aye, quiet enough to hear a septim drop in the marketplace. Though quiet never means safe in Solitude, does it, guard? Solitude Guard: Safe enough with the Jarl's steel watching the walls. What brings a scaled face like yours out at this hour, away from the docks? Jaree-Ra: Business never sleeps. A shipment arrives at dawn, and I like to count my coin before the sun shows its face. You understand profit, surely, even in that fancy armor. Solitude Guard: Armor keeps the blood in, Argonian. Profit keeps the city running. I respect both. Just make sure your business stays on the right side of the Keep. Jaree-Ra: Always, guard. I am a simple merchant, nothing more. The scent of sea salt and honest trade follows me wherever I wade. Solitude Guard: Honest trade. Right. I heard tell of a cargo ship that went missing near the Icewater Jetty last week. You wouldn't know anything about that, would you?

Solitude Guard: First light creeps over the stone. Still time for shadows to hide what they want hidden. Jaree-Ra: Shadows and light dance the same dance every morning, my scaled friend. One gives way to the other. Much like coin changing hands in the dark. Solitude Guard: That missing ship, Jaree-Ra. Three crew, all Argonian. Vanished between here and Dawnstar. You hear any whispers in the bilge? Jaree-Ra: Whispers are cheap in Solitude. Truth costs more than most can pay. But if your Jarl wants answers, maybe she should look at who owns the wharf contracts, not who scrubs the decks. Solitude Guard: Careful. That sounds like you know more than a simple merchant ought to. Jaree-Ra: I know only what the tide brings to my ears. And the tide says your missing vessel had debts. Heavy ones. To people who don't send polite letters. Solitude Guard: Debts to whom? Name them. Jaree-Ra: Names have power, guard. And power costs. What will you give me for a name that could save your investigation weeks of dead ends?

Solitude Guard: That torch you're holding casts a long shadow, Jaree-Ra. Makes it hard to see what you're really reaching for. Jaree-Ra: A torch lights the path for honest travelers and those who prefer the dark alike. I am merely admiring the stars. They look different from Solitude than from the swamps of Black Marsh. Solitude Guard: Different how? Jaree-Ra: In Black Marsh, the stars seem to drip down through the canopy, like dew on spider silk. Here, they stand guard, cold and distant.

(*You are observing the following:* A dark, nighttime scene unfolds in a cobblestone courtyard, framed by heavy stone architecture. In the center, a large, arched stone gateway serves as a focal point, shrouded in deep shadows. Above the entrance, a dark red banner hangs, featuring a pale emblem. Dim, warm light flickers from small windows and wall-mounted lanterns, casting a faint glow against the rough textures of the stone buildings. To the right, the silhouette of a gabled roofline sits heavily against the darkness. On the ground, a circular stone medallion or decorative inlay is embedded within the uneven cobblestones, catching a small amount of the ambient light. The overall atmosphere is somber and quiet, characterized by high-contrast shadows and a sense of ancient, fortified surroundings.)
